text:
Carla: Hi support — our CI has started failing deploys for the last hour. GitHub Actions runners return 401 from POST /v1/deploy with `token_expired` in the body. We rolled our ephemeral token TTL down to 5m yesterday to be more secure. Could that be the problem? :grimacing:

Sam: Hey Carla, can you paste the failing curl output and confirm which auth flow you're using (OIDC -> impersonation vs long-lived key)?

Carla: OIDC -> service-account impersonation. Here are the exact lines from the job run:

```
Run: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"image":"acme/service:pr-123"}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
X-Request-Id: abc123
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"token_expired","message":"token has expired or is not yet valid"}
```

Sam: That matches two common causes: (1) your TTL is too short and the job sits in queue/has pre-steps, so token is expired by use time, or (2) runner clock skew making iat/exp appear invalid. Also check impersonation window/ttl mismatch.

Priya: pinging infra to check NTP on runners — we've seen `not yet valid` come from clock skew before. @infra-bot can you run a quick sync check on eu-west runners?

infra-bot: running NTP sanity checks on eu-west runner pool. Return in about 2m. (automated)

Carla: Observed pattern: about 30% of jobs fail, mainly ones that sat in the queue >3 minutes. The token is acquired at job start, then we have build + lint steps that take a few minutes before deploy.

Sam: Sounds TTL-related. If expires_in is 5m at issuance but queue + steps consume 2–3m, your usable window is tiny. Quick mitigations: increase TTL to 15m for the impersonation assertion, or fetch a fresh token immediately before the deploy step. Long-term: request short-lived tokens as late as possible.

Dave: From security POV we prefer short lifetimes. If you increase TTL, do it for a scoped deploy-only service account that follows least privilege. We can approve 15m for a deploy SA that only has necessary permissions.

Carla: How can we quickly check token expiry inside the runner? I tried decoding the JWT but want a reliable command.

Sam: Use this to inspect exp delta (Linux/mac runners):

```
exp=$(echo "$REDWOOD_TOKEN" | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 --decode | jq -r '.exp')
now=$(date +%s)
echo "exp: $exp now: $now delta: $((exp - now)) seconds"
```

If delta <= 0 then expired. If delta < 120s, risky.

Priya: infra-bot update: runner clocks are within 2s of NTP. So skew isn't the root cause.

Carla: Ok we'll try TTL first. We control the IdP so we can set `expires_in` when minting. Will bump to 15m and test.

Sam: Note: also verify whether your deployer caches tokens. We saw a case where a process cached a token for 10m and reused it past expiry. That bites in CI.

Carla: That was us — deployer caches tokens for 10m by default. I'll change it to fetch per-deploy and set a small in-memory cache (60s) to avoid hammering IdP.

Priya: infra action item: can support engineering add a more informative error or dev debug header? Right now body is `token_expired`. If API emitted `X-Auth-Exp` header in staging it would help customers see server time vs token exp. @Sam can you open an infra request?

Sam: File INF-2043 to add an optional `X-Auth-Exp` header in staging logs for a short window. That should make diagnosing expiry vs skew straightforward.

Carla: After increasing to 15m we ran three deploys with the usual pre-steps — no 401s so far. We'll also provision a deploy-only SA with least-privilege. Dave, what exact permissions should that SA have?

Dave: Grant only `deploys.create`, `models.read`, and `secrets.get`. Avoid `secrets.list` and any `admin.*` roles. We'll add an audit rule if the SA's scopes are modified. I'll open SEC-778 to provision the SA and attach a draft policy for review.

Sam: Extra tips: if you cannot change TTL, add a quick pre-warm noop call right before heavy steps to ensure the token was recently used/validated. Or request a fresh token in the final deploy job.

Carla: We'll do both: bump TTL temporarily, create scoped SA, and remove long caching. Thanks all. Will update when SEC-778 is ready and after the next deploy batch. :pray:

Priya: Marking triaged. If failures persist after SA swap and pipeline adjustments, escalate to oncall. Thanks team.
